items.title: A cut cable disrupted hundreds of flights across the US
items.summary: A JetBlue airplane past an FAA air traffic control tower at Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, US, on Friday, Oct. 24, 2025. JetBlue Airways Corp. is expected to release earnings figures on October 28. Photographer: Ryan Collerd/Bloomberg via Getty Images | Bloomberg via Getty Images Hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed on Monday after construction crews in New Jersey accidentally cut a Verizon fiber cable used for air traffic control. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that a circuit failure led to the discovery of the severed fiber cable, ABC News reports. The outage hammered airports across the Northeast, causing ground stops at all three major New York City airports. In a statement to CNBC, Verizon said that it bore "no responsibility for this incident," putting the blame on "construction contractors working in the area" that "dug up and cut our cable." items.title: Black Tesla employees accuse company of fostering racial discrimination in major trial
items.summary: Lawyers say Black employees at Tesla experienced ‘rampant racism’ that was left unchecked for years at their flagship factory in California Dozens of Black employees at Tesla’s flagship plant in California said they were subject to racist slurs, unequal pay and promotions, and bullying by supervisors on a daily basis, a situation management did little to nothing to fix. Their complaints form the basis of a lawsuit brought against the Elon Musk-owned electric car company by the state of California, which began trial with opening statements on Monday. items.summary: Shooting of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez comes months after increased federal immigration enforcement in Austin The Venezuelan man who was shot by a federal immigration officer in Texas on Sunday spoke out from detention on Monday afternoon when he was able to call his lawyer, in the middle of a press conference, and plead for better medical care. Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was taken from a hospital in Austin into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention, even though he apparently still has a bullet lodged near his spine and is in much discomfort. items.title: Young people’s Pip claims for ADHD and autism ‘rising fastest in affluent areas’
items.summary: Experts say trend across England probably reflects swifter access to diagnoses as wealthier families go private Some of the most affluent areas of England have had the sharpest rises in the proportion of young people claiming disability benefits for ADHD and autism since the pandemic, according to new research. Claims for the personal independence payment (Pip) benefit for these health conditions were typically proportionally far higher in deprived areas with higher rates of poverty, low educational outcomes and insecure employment. items.title: Appeals court rules in favor of Trump-backed Missouri congressional maps
items.summary: Supreme court, which has twice blocked maps from being used in November, likely to have final say in legal fight A long-running legal fight over Missouri’s congressional map took another turn Monday when a federal appeals panel ruled in favor of new districts backed by Donald Trump, even though the US supreme court has blocked those districts from being used in the November election. A three-judge panel of the 8th US circuit court of appeals said Missouri should use the new Republican-drawn US House districts in the November election, just as the state did in its August primary. To revert to its prior districts for the general election would violate the US constitution, the appeals judges said. Continue reading...

items.summary: 공무원을 사칭해 접근한 뒤 노인을 상대로 금품을 빼앗은 30대 여성이 구속됐다.제주 서귀포경찰서는 30대 여성을 강도 혐의로 구속했다고 22일 밝혔다. 여성은 19일 오후 5시 31분경 서귀포시 보목동의 주택에서 80대 여성이 목에 걸고 있던 금목걸이를 빼앗아 달아난 혐의를 받는다.이 여성은 “공무원인데 어르신 건강 상태를 점검하러 왔다”고 속인 뒤 접근한 것으로 파악됐다. 금목걸이는 700만~800만 원 상당으로 알려졌다. 경찰은 인근 폐쇄회로(CC)TV 등을 통해 여성을 검거했다.한편 경찰은 정확한 사건 경위와 추가 범행 여부 등을 조사하고 있다.

items.summary: 웹툰 ‘쌉니다 천리마마트’ 등을 연재한 김규삼 작가가 추석을 앞두고 화실 직원들에게 한우 세트를 선물했지만 상태가 좋지 못해 난감해진 사연을 공개했다. 김 작가는 21일 자신이 관리하는 네이버웹툰 커뮤니티 게시판에 “화실 식구들에게 명절 선물로 16만9000원짜리 한우 세트를 돌렸는데 이런 물건이 배송됐다”며 “못 먹는 기름덩어리와 진공이 풀려서 변색돼 있어서 받은 사람이 곤란해하다가 알려주는 일이 생겼다”고 올렸다. 실제로 김 작가가 공개한 첫번째 사진 속 소고기는 선홍빛 살코기 부분을 찾아보기 힘들다. 또 다른 사진에선 일부 소고기가 변색돼 있는 모습을 확인할 수 있었다.김 작가는 “판매자는 해명도 안 해준다. 고객센터에 문의하려니까 챗봇이 뺑뺑이만 돌리니까 약만 오르고 있었다”면서도 “갑자기 천리마마트 현금선물 세트가 생각나서 혼자서 좀 웃었다. 앞으로는 그냥 선물 같은 거 안 돌리고 돈으로 보내기로 했다”고 전했다. ‘천리마마트’는 김 작가가 연재한 웹툰이다. 이후 김 작

items.title: “택시비 나중에 주겠다” 흉기로 기사 협박한 20대 체포
items.summary: 요금 시비 끝에 흉기로 택시 기사를 협박한 20대 승객이 경찰에 붙잡혔다.전북 완주경찰서는 특수협박 혐의로 20대를 조사 중이라고 21일 밝혔다.이 20대는 전날 오후 6시 10분경 완주군 봉동읍의 한 아파트에서 자신이 가지고 있던 흉기로 택시 기사(70대)를 협박한 혐의를 받는다.당시 승객은 돈이 없다며 나중에 계좌로 이체하겠다고 했고, 택시 기사는 이를 거절했다. 이후 실랑이가 붙자 승객이 가방에 있던 흉기를 꺼낸 것으로 전해졌다.신고를 받고 출동한 경찰은 20대를 현행범으로 체포했다.경찰은 정확한 사건 경위를 조사 중이다.

items.title: “사람이 떠있어요” 부천 굴포천서 30대 남성 시신 발견
items.summary: 경기 부천의 한 하천에서 30대가 숨진 채 발견됐다.22일 경찰과 소방 등에 따르면 전날 오전 9시 25분경 부천시 오정구 삼정동 굴포천에 사람이 떠있는 것 같다는 신고가 접수됐다. 출동한 경찰과 소방당국은 물에 떠있는 남성을 발견해 인양했으나 이미 사망한 상태였다.경찰은 지문 감식을 통해 시신의 신원을 30대로 확인했다. 시신에선 외상이나 범죄 혐의점은 확인되지 않은 것으로 파악됐다.경찰은 시신을 국립과학수사연구원에 보내 부검을 의뢰하고 정확한 사인과 사망 경위 등을 확인할 방침이다.

items.title: 전국 오존주의보 발령 48일…폭염에도 10년 평균 밑돌아
items.summary: 올해 여름 폭염에도 전국 오존주의보 발령일 수는 예년보다 줄어든 것으로 나타났다. 특히 8월과 남부권에서 감소폭이 두드러졌는데, 일사량과 강수일 등 오존 생성에 불리한 기상 조건이 영향을 미친 것으로 분석됐다.기후에너지환경부 소속 국립환경과학원은 오존 고농도 시기인 5월부터 8월까지 전국 오존주의보 발령 현황을 분석한 결과 이같이 나타났다고 22일 밝혔다.올해 5~8월 전국 오존주의보 발령일 수는 48일로 2016년 이후 장기간 장마가 이어진 2020년(40일)에 이어 두 번째로 적었다. 최근 3년간 발령일 수도 2024년 61일, 지난해 54일, 올해 48일로 감소했다. 월별로는 8월의 감소폭이 가장 컸다. 올해 8월 발령일 수는 10일로 2016~2025년 평균인 13.7일보다 3.7일(27%) 줄었다. 2024년 21일과 비교하면 절반 이상인 11일(52.4%) 감소했다.지역별 발령일 수는 수도권 27일, 중부권 16일, 남부권 17일, 동남권 23일이었다. 최근 10년

items.title: AI 쓰는 직장인 10명 중 6명 “일자리 안 줄어*
items.summary: 생성형 인공지능(AI) 활용 가능성이 높은 직업의 재직자 10명 중 6명은 AI 도입 이후 조직 내 같은 직업군의 인력 규모에 변화가 없다고 응답한 것으로 나타났다.국회예산정책처는 22일 이 같은 내용을 담은 ‘생성형 AI의 노동시장 영향’ 보고서를 발간했다.해당 보고서에 따르면, ‘화이트칼라’ 중심 57개 직업 재직자 1512명을 대상으로 실시한 설문조사에서 생성형 AI를 업무에 활용한다는 응답은 76.1%로 나타났다.이번 조사는 생성형 AI를 일상 업무에 활용할 가능성이 있는 직업을 중심으로 진행됐다. 업무상 AI 활용률이 낮은 육체노동 중심 직종과 군인 등 일부 직업은 조사 대상에서 제외됐다.조사에서 AI 도입 이후 조직 내 자신과 같은 직업군의 인력 규모가 어떻게 달라졌는지 묻는 질문에는 62.6%가 ‘변화 없음’이라고 답했다. ‘줄었다’는 응답은 15.3%, ‘늘었다’는 답변은 13.6%로 집계됐다.또한 AI 사용자들이 답한 업무 처리량 증가율은 평균 21.2%로

items.title: 최근 5년 새 ‘기간제’ 담임 31% 급증…“정규교원 감축 여파”

items.title: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use
items.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom has signed seven bills designed to prevent AI data centers from passing utility costs onto residents, as reported earlier by the Los Angeles Times. items.summary: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it's planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids. items.title: Can John Ternus find Apple’s next big thing?
items.summary: Today, I’m talking with Mark Gurman, who is the world’s best-sourced Apple reporter — both as Bloomberg’s chief Apple correspondent and the host of the upcoming podcast Power On. Earlier this month, Apple hosted its annual iPhone hardware event, virtually every detail of which was reported ahead of time by Mark. But this event was special, for a number of reasons. It was new Apple CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch since he took over for former CEO Tim Cook less than two weeks prior. It was also the debut of the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable smartphone. The timing of those two things was not at all coincidental, as you’ll hear Mark explain. Apple takes these hardware events — and the stories they tell — extremely seriously. This year’s story actually says a great deal about what’s happening at Apple, how Cook managed in wholesale leadership ranks over the past year, and how all of that might change Apple’s culture. Furthermore, what all that tells about Ternus’ plan to navigate Apple from what you might call the iPhone era into the AI era. Okay: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman on the future of Apple. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Mark Gurman, you’re the chief Apple correspondent and the managing editor of consumer technology at Bloomberg. Welcome to Decoder. Good to be here finally. Thanks for having me. And it’s been a while, so it’s good to catch up on all things Apple. Yeah, I’m really excited to talk to you. Obviously, Apple just had its big event. They announced the iPhone Duo. It was John Ternus’s first event as CEO. This is a Decoder episode, so we’ve got a new CEO, and we’ve got a new org chart inside of Apple. There’s been a lot of shuffling. You’ve been chronicling them very, very deeply over the past few years. Let’s just start with the event. I have a very basic question for you. Sure. Do you ever get nostalgic for a time when you didn’t know what was going to happen at the iPhone event? Do I ever get nostalgic? Do you ever wish that you, Mark Gurman, were about to be surprised? Honestly, I never think about it that way. I’m just fixated on delivering the goods and delivering the news. And people love their Apple. People want to know everything that’s coming down to the last minute, so I’m here to provide it for them. The thing with me, and I don’t know if most people know this about me, but I hope people know this about me, is that I’m a huge Apple fan through and through, and I’ve always been. And I’m so lucky to be able to cover a company that I love, a company that I am obsessed with, and a company whose products I use. There are so many people who cover companies that they couldn’t care less about. That’s not me. So I do what I do because I love Apple and I love covering Apple. I love the community around it, and I love talking about it. And it’s always fun to get a peek at the future and help keep not only myself informed, but people informed around me. That actually leads me to a lot of things because I’ve known you forever. We’ve been working in and around the same spaces forever. You got your start as an Apple blogger at the Apple rumor sites. There’s a whole culture around Apple that has grown up and changed over the years, and you can trace it to different eras of hardware, to different CEOs, to different sizes of the company. This was the first event with John Ternus as CEO. Apple announced a big new product in the iPhone Duo. Do you sense that the community is changing? How do you think that community has changed over the years? And do you think Ternus is going to lead to a difference in what that community feels like? I have to say, this event really didn’t feel much different than a Tim Cook event. They felt pretty interchangeable. It could have been Tim up there introducing it. It could have been Ternus up there introducing it. The one thing I will say that did feel slightly different is that Ternus came out swinging with a point of view on AI. The first thing he came out with was about the intelligent personal hub. Now, here’s the big difference between Tim Cook and John Ternus in terms of their management style. You’re inside Apple, you’re an executive, you’ll come to him with an idea, you’ll come to him with a viewpoint, a decision, an opinion, and he’ll just pepper you with more questions. He won’t make a singular decision in many cases. It’s very much communal decision-making, collaborative decision-making. John Ternus, if you come to him and you want him to make a decision, he’ll make a decision. He’ll have an opinion. Now, you may hate his opinion; you may completely disagree with him, but he has a viewpoint. But that’s the big difference between talking to people about Ternus and Tim. Ternus comes out talking about his view on AI. I may disagree with it. A lot of people may disagree with it. They may think the OpenAI or Anthropic approach is superior, but at least he came out and had a viewpoint. Apple’s been at this AI game now for two years since they launched Apple Intelligence at WWDC in 2024, and it’s been a mishmash of things. They haven’t really come out with a very strong narrative and viewpoint, and they finally did. So, as I said, whether you agree with it or not, they did do that. And I thought that was a really interesting way to kick off the keynote. All right, we’re just going to get into the weeds of Apple nerds disagreeing about things. Okay, let’s do it. I sat through that event, and I appreciated the same thing that you saw, which is, “Oh, we’re telling a story.” John Ternus is on the stage, and the first thing he’s doing is telling a story about this product and how it fits into the universe of technology. And then I took a beat, and I was like, oh, but they’re also just making sure that he’s successful at his first event by playing Apple’s greatest hits. Because an “intelligent personal hub” is just a replay of Steve Jobs saying the iMac was the digital hub. At the very end of the event, Ternus said, “There’s one more thing, and it’s the iPhone Duo.” There was just a part of all of that that, to me, felt like Apple saying, “Look, our new CEO can put on the clothes of the old CEO. He can do this same dance that you’re expecting.” Underneath it, what I felt was, to your point, that I don’t buy the story about the intelligent hub. No, I don’t buy it either. Because any of the things we’re seeing AI do are happening in cloud services. It’s the same week that Meta launched Muse, right? Right. You can feel what you want about Meta launching Muse, but Mark Zuckerberg is giving everybody 8GB of storage and 8GB of RAM in the cloud, and Muse can go do a lot of things that AI on the iPhone absolutely cannot do at this point in time. I just felt like there was a part where they were playing it really safe with John by having him basically show up and be the new lead singer of Journey. You can’t get it wrong if you’re going to do “Lights.” If you’re going to show up on stage and do “Don’t Stop Believin’,” you’re going to be fine for a minute. And it’s all the stuff that comes after that’s going to really show his real personality. But it sounds like you thought that that’s his point of view. Well, it’s a couple of things. At a very high level, Apple’s going to tell a story around what they have. If Apple invented ChatGPT, they would’ve invented ChatGPT, and they would’ve told a good story around that. Apple has gone as far as it’s able to, at least for now, on AI. So it’s telling the story, the best version of that story that they can with what they have to work with, with the bird they have in hand. So that’s the one thing. I agree with you on the intelligent personal hub, and how that compares to the iMac back in ’98. And it feels like they’re trying to sell this pivot from the Mac as the center of everything with the peripherals around it; then you got to iCloud in 2011, the center of everything with the peripherals around it. Now, it’s this Intelligence right at the center with everything around it. But what’s so fascinating is that Apple held a major product launch event in September of the year 2026 and did not introduce a single notable new AI feature. The first 15 minutes or so of the keynote was simply a replay, a re-narrativization of what they introduced over the past two years with Apple Intelligence. And so they tried to just tell that story in a more concrete way. The other thing is they don’t have any AI devices at the very core, and so they need to prop up the iPhone as their AI device because they don’t have an alternative. But of course they’re only going to do that until they have that killer device, and then they’re going to change that whole narrative. So it’s a very narrative PR and marketing-driven company. And I’m not saying that to be critical. I mean, if I ran the company, obviously I’m going to tout what I have. I’m not going to veer from that. But it is interesting how they’re playing this. And I agree, they did play it very safe. There’s nothing safer than John Ternus introducing a new iPhone. It’s like the safest thing you can do. No major new AI product, no smart home hub, nothing in the spatial space, just straight down the middle. Yeah, it seems like that next wave of smart home products, which we’re expecting later this year… I say, “We’re expecting.” I’m expecting it because that is something you have reported. [Laughs] I am expecting it, yes. Mark Gurman is expecting new products from Apple. That is the first cut at some truly AI-native devices. Because you have Siri AI and it is functional now in a way that it previously was not functional, you can try some new classes of devices. There are about a half dozen AI-native devices coming in the next year and a half or so. The first will be the smart home hub, which is basically an Amazon Echo Show but Apple-style. It will have a square screen and an entirely new operating system. The idea is: what would a Siri AI operating system look like? This is that: intercom, video conferencing, proactive intelligence. So you walk up to it, it recognizes who you are, and it will show content personal to you. It will know who is speaking. Obviously, the Amazon Echo can do that, but Apple’s doing it in its own Apple-y way with AI-based Face ID. They’re working on a home security system. They’re working on another version of the smart home hub that I just talked about that is attached to a robotic arm. So you put it on your desk, and it can move around. It’s actually a category that’s pretty popping in Asia and in China right now. Then you’ve got the wearables, the smart glasses. I still believe those are going to be introduced and shipped in 2027, so not too far from now. Trust me, you’ll be wearing them. Within 365 days, you will be wearing them and have video footage of you wearing them at the Steve Jobs Theater. And if that is not the case, either something went horribly wrong for you or something went horribly wrong for Apple. You’ll also have the AirPods with cameras. That’s an interesting thing that we should talk about, but they’ll have the AirPods with cameras and then a few other wearables that I won’t get into. So this is what I was talking about when I said there were eras at Apple and people’s relationship with the company really changed. The Steve Jobs era was defined by devices, and in particular, Steve Jobs himself getting up and doing a keynote and famously putting up pictures of all the existing smartphones and saying, “Well, these all suck. And here’s the reason they all suck, and here’s the iPhone and here’s why it’s better.” That created one kind of relationship between Apple’s enormous community of fans, its leader, and the products. I think that was very successful. I think the Tim Cook era has been meaningfully different. I think it’s largely a story about scale. To some extent, it’s a story about values. To a huge extent, it’s a story about privacy. Apple has marketed itself as the privacy company. It fought the FBI to keep the iPhone encrypted. There’s a lot there with Tim Cook’s version of the company, but it’s more corporate. Certainly, it’s just a vaster company. It’s safer. It’s not as rough around the edges as Jobs’ Apple, but it wasn’t as device-based. I don’t think the Vision Pro has the same kind of mainstream cultural impact as even the hockey puck mouse that Jobs put out. There was a thing that he could do with products that Tim Cook Apple could not quite do with products. And that just feels really different to me. I’m going to correct you on that because every time I put an article or a post out about the Vision Pro being on life support, I get what amounts to basically a notch or two below a death threat from dozens of people. So people are passionate about it. Dozens? Dozens? Well, honestly, I think what it is is that people have created businesses around spatial computing and apps, and they’re just pissed off that they’ve invested all this time and money in a category that’s probably going to die out. And then you have consumers who spent four grand on this product, and they’re like, “I saved up for this thing, I’m living with this thing, and I’m pissed off to hear the realities.” But if you have another hour, we can talk about the Vision Pro. No, the comparison there is good. People have invested in it. They care deeply about it. The comparison I’m making is that the relationship people have to Apple in the Cook era is as an institution. It’s just like this big thing that spans the globe on a massive scale. It’s IBM. Yeah, and in the Jobs era, it was all about really, really innovative new products that redefined categories over and over again. You’re describing a whole bunch of new products that came up in the Cook era that John Ternus is going to launch. How do you expect the culture of Apple to change around its products or its relationship to the culture to change as we go from one CEO to another? But think about what they did. You’ve got the coolest new iPhone and Apple product in maybe 10, 20 years introduced one week after Tim Cook steps down. And then for the next 12 to 18 months, you’ve got, I don’t know, six or seven new product categories. Maybe you have 25 pretty breakthrough things. So Tim Cook made a decision that, even though his tenure at a product company was pretty limited in major new things, the Apple Watch turned out to be a success, even though it started as a complete dud, as you remember. The AirPods are a unique beast in that they’re an accessory, but it’s not a platform on its own yet. It’s going to get there. And the Vision Pro is a failure. Tim Cook could have ended his tenure as CEO with the iPhone Duo. He could have just waited. Typical transitions at Apple happen mid-October or mid-April; they happen on January 1st. It was a specific decision that was made for John Ternus to be the one to introduce the iPhone Duo. It was a specific decision made for John Ternus to be the one to introduce this whole new product roadmap. Even though, as you know, because of the length of hardware development cycles and R&D, these things were in the oven for five to 10 years. So it’s really interesting that this decision was made to let Ternus be the face of this whole new era of products rather than allow Tim Cook to take the credit for it. And I think that’s to your point where they’re trying to draw the line in the sand of this new era. If Cook is already going to step down in the next three years, let’s just do it now and let Ternus take the credit for everything. Take me inside that. You’ve obviously done a lot of reporting. I think you were the first to break the news that Cook would be searching for a successor. You were, I think, among the very first to break that it would be Ternus. Tell me about that process. This is a big decision; Cook is going to play a huge role at the company. He has a massive compensation program tied pretty much to having to talk to Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. It seems like that’s his job: to just manage that relationship. For $47 million a year, I would talk to Trump and Xi Jinping on the phone every day. [Laughs] I would need at least 50, but that’s just me. That’s his job: to go do politics much the same way that Eric Schmidt at Google was in charge of governments after Larry Page became CEO. There’s a whole pattern here. Brad Smith at Microsoft, even though he wasn’t CEO, but yeah. He’s the president of the company. Yeah, there’s a parallel here. Tell me about this decision of Tim Cook wanting to elevate his position to something like that, and of making John Ternus the face of the product side of the company in this new role. So 2023 rolls around and Tim Cook starts every executive team meeting, all high-level meetings with people at Apple at the executive levels, with, “We need to start taking succession seriously. We need to start thinking about who the next people are.” At that time, there was a really strong realization that many of the people at the top of Apple either had half a billion dollars in the bank or were already billionaires, and that this era would start to age out really quickly. And so Tim Cook knew that he wanted to take a step back. Jeff Williams, the number two as the COO, knew he wanted to retire. The CFO, Luca Maestri, wanted to retire, too. The general counsel, Kate Adams, also wanted to retire. They were all about the same age, give or take a few years. So they basically came up with this plan that would go one by one over the next few years. It started with the CFO. Luca retires at the very end of 2024, and he’s replaced by the new CFO, Kevan Parekh. Then 2025 rolls around, and Jeff Williams, the COO, retires and is replaced by his deputy, Sabih Khan. Then in 2026, they had the transition for the general counsel, and they got a great replacement for her from Meta, Jennifer Newstead. And then at the end of 2026, the big one: Tim Cook to John Ternus. So they played this out very, very slowly. You’re going to get people mad about this, and then you’re going to do the next one the next time. Right. It just seems like this next generation of devices involves some kind of ambient listening that we are not ready for as a society. People are really mad about Meta glasses. What are you going to do about it? They soiled the water for Apple and a lot of other companies. Meta being the first mover on this created an industry-wide problem. And I think even though Apple has such a strong privacy stance, there are people who don’t believe them. There are people who don’t care what they have to say. There are people who are going to be angry about the Apple glasses and whatnot. I think Apple, to some extent, is on such a high horse with its privacy message that it came away surprised that there would be some backlash to Apple doing this. They think, I believe, that people are overblowing it when it comes to Apple and everyone should just be focused on Meta. And just because Meta has done a poor job protecting people’s privacy doesn’t mean we’re going to. So we’ll see what happens. One thing: when I talk to the folks there, they never make the connection between Apple and Meta in the sense that Meta’s apps run on Apple’s phones. People are mad about Meta, and they still think the phones, Apple’s phones, are listening to them, and they can’t quite make that connection because it undoes a lot of their own messaging. If you believe your iPhone is listening to you, that’s not just Meta’s problem. It is also Apple’s problem. They kind of have to actively ignore that relationship because otherwise everything else falls apart. And I think that’s why there’s this blind spot. If people’s watches start generating transcripts, it’s exactly the same relationship as “my iPhone is listening to me, and that’s why I saw an ad for a vacation that I only talked to my friend about.” I’m curious what they’re going to do. I have a feeling they’re just going to bulldoze their way through it. They’re going to just try to tell a good story. They’re going to do a ton of PR briefings about it. They’re going to do a ton of white papers about it, and get as nerdy and in-depth as they can on this stuff. You know what they’re going to do? They’re going to throw out a lot of comparisons. I even heard Ternus do this in one of the interviews, in Apple’s statement on some of these features. I could totally imagine them saying, “Why is it any different recording from smart glasses if you could just hold your phone up and record people?” With the audio intelligence feature, one thing I didn’t even think of is the Apple Watch- It’s very funny you just mentioned that because that is exactly what Mark Zuckerberg just said to our friend Alex Heath. Oh, that’s funny. “How is it different from a phone?” This is the industry’s approach. I think the answer is that people are like, “Yeah, I can see you doing that, and I feel very comfortable telling you to stop.” There’s something different about that. I didn’t even realize this. Someone pointed this out to me the other day. It’s like your Apple Watch has had the Voice Memos app for, I don’t know, eight years at this point. Who stopped anyone from recording their whole day with the Voice Memos app on the Apple Watch anyway? This is just a more privacy-centric version of that. So Apple’s solving a problem here. They’re not creating one. So it just depends on how you look at these things. I think they’ll bulldoze their way through it. It’s going to be a problem, but I think they’ll be fine. All right. Last two before I let you get out of here. We’ve talked around the iPhone Duo a lot. We’ve mentioned it a lot. It’s the thing that just came out. We haven’t talked about it. What do you think of it? I think it’s incredible. I think, and this is a bold take, that foldables will become the new normal within a decade. If you look at the market share of smartphones at the end of 2006, smartphones had like 6 percent of the market. Now they have 85 percent of the market. It went over 50 percent of the market after five to six years. The iPhone itself was not the source of that, but the iPhone got everyone into the smartphone game. I think the iPhone Duo is going to do the same for the phone market. I think it’s going to become the new normal. Even though Apple is a late mover to foldables? Yeah. I think the Apple brand is that strong, really. I really do. I think the fit and finish, the software integration, is going to get people really excited about this category. I think that the Apple Upgrade program, the leasing program, will eventually expand internationally. I think that’s going to get people in it. I think that at some point they’re going to stop advertising sticker prices and focus on the monthly prices, and they’re going to get people locked into this thing. They’re going to have a family of iPhone Duos over time. You’ll see every phone maker just transitioning, transitioning to foldables. Samsung: half the line is already foldables. Very soon the candy bar style is going to become legacy. That’s a big prediction. Although I will say their iPhone handoff feature, where you can move a number between phones, seems to point to a future where I, for example, have the folding phone for work and then a much smaller, lighter phone for the weekends with the family. You can see that vision taking shape only because it’s now easy to port a number between devices, just whenever you want, which I think is incredible. Last question. We’ve talked a lot about Apple, its culture, and its set of products. What do you think its biggest challenges are in the new era under John Ternus, and what do you think its biggest opportunities are? I would say that I think the biggest challenge and the biggest opportunity are the same thing. Ternus’ Apple for the next three to five years is still Tim Cook’s Apple, right? That’s just the reality. He’s still going to be there in the background. He’s still going to loom large, and the product pipeline is still going to be coming out of an era that started under Tim Cook. But in five years from now, they are going to need to start thinking of what actually replaces the iPhone as the next thing. We went from the Mac to iCloud to AI as the center. What is Apple’s new thing after the phone? What is Apple’s new thing after the current generation of AI? And Ternus’ tenure as CEO, I think, will go down as a success if he’s able to find that next new centerpiece. He’s got a few years before he needs to start cooking on that, but I’m talking about something that can be in development for 5 to 10 years. Tim Cook never had the opportunity to have his new centerpiece of the company. He never had the opportunity to put his stamp on products at the company for two reasons. Both things that he tried to do as his centerpiece failed spectacularly. Obviously the Vision Pro, but the car — the car, that was Apple’s multi-trillion-dollar market cap opportunity, and they just blew it. Ternus will need to successfully hit that. I’d actually put a third thing on that list. It was the very beginning of the Cook era, with Jobs literally on his deathbed, and he said he’d figured out TV. Oh, yes. He had to spend however long pretending he knew what that meant because I don’t think it had been solved. And so there was this first wave of “Apple’s going to redefine TV” because the last page of the Isaacson biography had a Jobs quote on it. They haven’t even done a new Apple TV box in four years. That’s a long time. It’s funny because you don’t need one. It never occurs to me that I need to upgrade this thing, but maybe there’s going to be some AI feature. Well, Siri AI. They’ve been waiting for the Siri AI update. This could be a whole other podcast, but Siri AI has been the gate to all of these new product categories. The AirPods were supposed to be out already, the Apple TV, the HomePod, the smart home hub… all these devices were supposed to come out. Apple couldn’t do any of them until Siri AI. Now Siri AI is here, so the floodgates are open. All right. Well, Mark, we’re going to have to have you back on the show to talk about those floodgates and all these new products very soon. I can’t believe you haven’t been on until now. Thank you so much for being on Decoder. Yeah. And obviously I’d love to have you on my new podcast, Power On Podcast, launching very shortly. So thanks in advance. Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!

items.title: The Guardian view on AI v mathematicians: humans are still vital to the field, but tech firms refuse to see that | Editorial
items.summary: OpenAI claims its agents have solved the Navier-Stokes problem. But questions remain about how useful and independent its work really is On 8 September, OpenAI claimed that its AI agents had solved the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the most famous and difficult challenges in mathematics. Had a human solved it, they would have collected both prize money and plaudits from their fellows. The announcement instead ignited what some mathematicians have called an “existential crisis” in their field over the power of AI, and accusations that OpenAI misused human work. The maths behind Navier-Stokes is difficult to understand, but the critiques levelled by mathematicians will be familiar to artists, office workers, or anyone else concerned about AI. OpenAI’s results, like any arising from a large language model, depend on digesting work by human mathematicians. The OpenAI paper cites sources, but many believe the company didn’t give sufficient credit, especially to several mathematicians believed to be very close to a solution – bad form that erases human ingenuity and hogs all the glory. The mathematician Tristan Buckmaster also has concerns that work he was doing on Navier-Stokes using OpenAI’s Codex model was seen by the OpenAI team. OpenAI has denied directly accessing this material, but could not rule out that data from Buckmaster’s use of their products “helped improve our model”. Continue reading...

articles.snippet: 육군 25사단 최전방 부대에서 21일 비무장지대(DMZ) 수색 작전 중 지뢰 폭발로 추정되는 폭발 사고가 발생했다.합동참모본부는 이날 “21일 오전 서부전선 비무장지대 MDL 이남 지점에서 작전을 수행하던 우리 군 간부 3명이 미상 폭발로 부상을 입었다”고 밝혔다.이어 “부상 간부 2명은 응급헬기를 이용해 국군수도병원으로 긴급 후송 및 치료 중”이라며 “부상 간부 1명을 포함해 작전을 수행했던 장병들도 국군수도병원으로 후송해 정밀 검진 등 건강 상태를 확인할 예정”이라고 덧붙였다.군 당국은 미상 폭발 원인에 대해서 조사할 예정이다.

articles.snippet: 방미 중인 이재명 대통령이 22일 이형일 부총리 겸 재정경제부 장관과 강신철 국방부 장관, 홍지선 국토교통부 장관에 대한 임명안을 재가했다. 청와대 강유정 수석대변인은 이날 공지를 통해 “이 대통령은 인사청문경과보고서가 채택된 이 장관과 강 장관, 홍 장관에 대한 임명안을 재가했다”며 이같이 전했다. 국회는 이 장관과 강 장관에 대한 청문 보고서를 17일 채택했다. 홍 장관에 대해서는 21일 채택됐다. 이소영 중소벤처기업부 장관 후보자에 대한 청문 보고서는 여야 이견으로 처리가 지연되고 있다.앞선 인사청문회에서 이 장관은 17년 보유한 경기 과천시 재건축 아파트에 약 4개월만 거주한 사실을 두고 ‘비거주 1주택’ 논란에 휩싸였다. 그는 당시 “국민 눈높이에 맞지 않아 송구하다”며 고개를 숙였다. 강 장관의 경우, 인사청문회에서 장남의 ‘이모 찬스’ 상가 매입 논란과 본인과 부친 등 일가족이 철거민 특별공급으로 서울 아파트를 취득한 것에 대한 논란이 이어졌다. 홍 장관에

articles.title: 李대통령, 미국 도착… 순방일정 시작 [청계천 옆 사진관]
articles.snippet: 이재명 대통령과 김혜경 여사가 21일(현지시간) 미국 뉴욕 JFK 국제공항에 도착했다. 공항에는 차지훈 주유엔대표부 대사 부부, 강경화 주미대사, 김상호 주뉴욕 총영사 부부 등이 나와 이 대통령 부부를 맞이했다.이재명 대통령은 현지시간 22일 오후 유엔총회장에서 기조연설을 실시한다. 이 대통령은 기조연설을 통해서 글로벌 문제 해결을 위한 유엔 개혁의 방향과 대한민국의 기여 방안을 제시하는 한편 한반도 평화 공존의 청사진에 대해서도 설명할 예정이다. 이어 이 대통령은 유엔 사무총장과 면담을 갖고 한반도 평화를 위한 유엔 차원의 관심과 협조를 당부할 계획이다.또한 미국, 호주 등 주요국 정상들과 다양한 방식의 별도 접촉이 있을 예정이다. 이를 통해, 긴밀한 정상 간 교류를 이어나가고 우리 국익을 확대하기 위한 협력 방안을 논의할 예정이다.

articles.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 “강남불패, 부동산 투기 공화국은 이제 과거 이야기가 될 것”이라고 22일 밝혔다.이 대통령은 이날 X(엑스·옛 트위터)에 “반드시 그래야 한다”며 이 같이 올렸다. 유엔총회 참석차 미국 뉴욕에 도착한 직후 게시물을 올린 것으로 보인다. 이와 함께 전날 정부가 발표한 이재명 정부의 첫 주거복지 대책인 ‘주거안정플랜’ 브리핑 영상을 공유했다. 이에 따르면 정부는 2030년까지 공공임대, 공공분양 등 공적주택 119만 채를 공급한다. 이 중 77%인 92만 채는 수도권에 집중한다. 중산층도 최대 20년 거주할 수 있는 ‘보편형 공공임대’를 도입한다.이 대통령은 그간 부동산 시장 정상화 의지를 강조해 왔다. 앞서 18일 청와대 영빈관에서 열린 기자회견에선 “대한민국의 부동산 투기 공화국 탈출은 이 정부의 가장 중심 과제”라며 “건축 허가를 포함한 택지 개발 또는 재건축, 재개발, 도시 정비 등 공급을 최대한 신속하게 늘려 나갈 것”이라고 했다. 지난달 30일에는 X에

articles.title: 한미일 외교장관 “北의 완전한 비핵화에 대한 의지 재확인”
articles.snippet: 한국과 미국, 일본의 외교장관들이 북한의 완전 비핵화 의지를 다시 한번 확인하는 한편 관련해 북한이 대화를 재개할 것을 촉구했다. 또 주로 중국을 겨냥한 것으로 해석되는 공급망 교란과 비시장 정책에 대해 “단호히 반대한다”는 메시지를 밝혔다.조현 외교부 장관과 마코 루비오 미 국무장관, 모테기 도시미쓰(茂木敏充) 일본 외무상은 21일(현지 시간) 유엔총회가 열리는 뉴욕에서 3자 회담을 하고 이 같은 내용의 공동성명을 발표했다.최근 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 김정은 북한 국무위원장과의 대화 의지를 거듭 밝힌 가운데 성명에서 3국 외교장관들은 북한 관련 문제를 가장 먼저 거론했다. 장관들은 “북한의 완전한 비핵화와 북한의 핵·탄도미사일 프로그램 자금 조달 금지에 대한 확고한 의지를 재확인했다”면서도 “대화의 길은 여전히 ​​열려 있음을 재확인하고, 한반도의 평화와 안정을 증진하기 위한 노력을 지속하는 한편, 북한이 대화를 재개할 것을 촉구했다”고 밝혔다. 또 납치범과 억류자, 미송

articles.title: ‘인사 책임’ 떠안고… 강훈식 비서실장 전격 사의
articles.snippet: 강훈식 대통령비서실장이 21일 이재명 대통령에게 사의를 표명했다고 밝혔다. 김승원 전 법무부 장관 후보자 낙마 등 8·30 개각 과정에서 인사 추천 및 검증 문제에 총체적 책임을 지고 물러나겠다는 것. 이 대통령은 “아직 어떻게 할지 결정을 못 하겠다”고 했다. 국민의힘은 강 실장 사퇴를 두고 “성남 라인 비선 실세의 책임을 은폐하는 카드”라고 비판했다. 성기홍 대통령홍보소통수석비서관은 이날 오후 1시 긴급 브리핑을 통해 “강훈식 비서실장은 오늘 오전 이재명 대통령에게 사의를 표명했다”고 밝혔다. 이에 대해 청와대 관계자는 “대통령이 지난주 기자회견에서 국정을 바라보는 국민의 시선에 대해 자신의 부족함 탓이라고 수차례 말한 상황”이라며 “대통령을 보좌하는 비서실장으로서 종합적인 책임을 지는 차원에서 사의를 표명한 것”이라고 설명했다. 정치권에서는 이 대통령의 순방을 불과 4시간여 앞두고 청와대 2인자인 비서실장이 사의를 표명한 것은 이례적이라는 반응이 나온다. 지난달 30일 이

articles.snippet: 정부가 22일 국회에서 대미 투자 협상 보고에 나선다. 한미는 대미 원전 투자 등에 접점을 찾은 것으로 알려졌지만 알래스카 액화천연가스(LNG) 사업 등 일부 핵심 쟁점에선 아직 이견이 남은 것으로 알려졌다. 21일 국회에 따르면 정부는 22일 국회 산업통상자원중소벤처기업위원회와 재정경제기획위원회에 비공개로 대미투자 사업 보고를 진행한다. 정부 측은 이날 223억 달러(약 31조 원) 규모의 대미투자 1호 프로젝트인 텍사스주 엔시날 가스복합화력발전소 사업의 구체적인 내용에 대해 보고할 예정이다. 알래스카 LNG 사업과 미국 원전기업 웨스팅하우스 지분 협상과 관련해서도 미국 측 요구와 한국 측 대응 관련 상황을 공유할 것으로 전망된다. 다만 알래스카 LNG 사업 대미투자 프로젝트와 우산형 특수목적법인(SPV)을 통한 투자 프로젝트 손익 관리 등에 대한 쟁점을 두고 한미는 아직 합의를 이루지 못한 것으로 전해졌다. 도널드 트럼프 행정부는 알래스카 LNG 사업 투자를 추진한다는 문구

articles.snippet: 정부가 22일 국회에서 대미 투자 협상 보고에 나선다. 한미는 대미 원전 투자 등에 접점을 찾은 것으로 알려졌지만 알래스카 액화천연가스(LNG) 사업 등 일부 핵심 쟁점에선 아직 이견이 남은 것으로 알려졌다. 21일 국회에 따르면 정부는 22일 국회 산업통상자원중소벤처기업위원회와 재정경제기획위원회에 비공개로 대미투자 사업 보고를 진행한다. 정부 측은 이날 223억 달러(약 31조 원) 규모의 대미투자 1호 프로젝트인 텍사스주 엔시날 가스복합화력발전소 사업의 구체적인 내용에 대해 보고할 예정이다. 알래스카 LNG 사업과 미국 원전기업 웨스팅하우스 지분 협상과 관련해서도 미국 측 요구와 한국 측 대응 관련 상황을 공유할 것으로 전망된다. 다만 알래스카 LNG 사업 대미투자 프로젝트와 우산형 특수목적법인(SPV)을 통한 투자 프로젝트 손익 관리 등에 대한 쟁점을 두고 한미는 아직 합의를 이루지 못한 것으로 전해졌다. 도널드 트럼프 행정부는 알래스카 LNG 사업 투자를 추진한다는 문구

articles.title: 靑 참모진 전면개편 빨라질듯… 인사-정무-민정라인 교체 가능성
articles.snippet: 강훈식 대통령비서실장이 21일 사의를 표명하면서 이재명 정부 2기 청와대 개편이 빨라질 것이라는 전망이 나온다. 이 대통령은 강 실장 사의 수용 여부를 두고 고심 중인 가운데 3실장 및 주요 수석급 참모에 대한 대대적인 개편으로 이어질 수 있다는 관측이 나온다. 이날 청와대 내에서는 강 실장이 사의 표명 사실을 공개적으로 밝힌 만큼 이 대통령이 결국 사의를 수용할 가능성이 크다는 전망이 나왔다. 청와대 관계자는 “비서실장의 사의 표명 사실을 공개한 이상 교체는 기정사실 아니겠냐”며 “새 비서실장과 함께 청와대 개편을 논의할 것으로 보인다”고 했다. 여권에선 비서실장 후임으로 친명(친이재명)계 천준호 한준호 의원, 김민기 전 국회 사무총장 등이 거론되고 있다. 다만 이 대통령이 강 실장의 사의 수용 시기를 늦출 수 있다는 분석도 나온다. 강 실장의 사의가 수리되면 청와대 3실장 가운데 위성락 국가안보실장을 제외하고 비서실장과 정책실장이 동시에 공석이 되는 이례적인 상황이 발생하기

articles.title: “김승원 탄원서 쓴 보좌진, 국회서 회견 열어 폭로 계획했었다”
articles.snippet: 법무부 장관 후보직에서 사퇴한 더불어민주당 김승원 의원의 성추행과 음주운전 의혹 등을 담은 탄원서를 청와대에 전달한 김 의원의 전직 보좌관이 “사퇴 전날 김 의원을 만나 사퇴를 촉구했지만 김 의원이 여러 가지 변명을 하면서 사퇴 의사를 밝히지 않았다”고 밝혔다. 김 의원은 이 자리에서 탄원서를 작성한 또 다른 전직 보좌진의 ‘국회 소통관 공개 폭로 기자회견’ 계획을 전해 듣고 만남을 타진했으나 거절당한 것으로 전해졌다. 김 의원은 다음 날 긴급 기자회견을 열어 자진 사퇴했다. 청와대에 탄원서를 전달한 전직 보좌관은 21일 통화에서 “18일 김 의원에게 탄원서 내용에 대한 입장을 확인할 겸 만나자고 요청했고 김 의원이 받아들여 모처에서 만났다”고 밝혔다. 그는 이 자리에서 김 의원에게 탄원서를 작성한 또 다른 보좌진의 폭로 기자회견 계획을 전하며 “(성추행) 피해자가 있으니 사퇴하는 방법밖에 없다”고 말했다고 한다. 이에 대해 김 의원은 설득을 시도하면서 사퇴 의사는 밝히지 않았다

articles.title: Macron and Carney announce closer France-Canada ties amid Trump tensions
articles.snippet: Two leaders meet in French territory off Canada as Ottawa seeks stronger relations with EU while fighting trade war with US The leaders of France and Canada have pledged closer ties to grapple with rising geopolitical tensions, climate change and the erosion of democratic values, after ⁠they met in a ⁠French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast. The two leaders’ visit to Saint-Pierre ​and Miquelon – the first by a French president since 2014 and the first by a Canadian prime minister – came just weeks ⁠after Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands, as well as all of Canada and other countries in North America, covered by the US flag. articles.title: GM can’t ‘bring back’ Apple CarPlay because it never left
articles.snippet: Last week, GM announced a new software experience for its upcoming Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks, including a new look for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, the popular phone mirroring systems that the automaker made a big deal about removing from its electric vehicles in 2023. Naturally, this led to some confusion about whether GM was "bringing back" CarPlay and Android Auto to its vehicles. Yahoo Finance reported it that way, calling it an "about-face" by the automaker, while Apple Insider's headline boasted that GM "cave[d]" on its decision to remove the interface from its gas-powered vehicles. articles.title: Can John Ternus find Apple’s next big thing?
articles.snippet: Today, I’m talking with Mark Gurman, who is the world’s best-sourced Apple reporter — both as Bloomberg’s chief Apple correspondent and the host of the upcoming podcast Power On. Earlier this month, Apple hosted its annual iPhone hardware event, virtually every detail of which was reported ahead of time by Mark. But this event was special, for a number of reasons. It was new Apple CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch since he took over for former CEO Tim Cook less than two weeks prior. It was also the debut of the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable smartphone. The timing of those two things was not at all coincidental, as you’ll hear Mark explain. Apple takes these hardware events — and the stories they tell — extremely seriously. This year’s story actually says a great deal about what’s happening at Apple, how Cook managed in wholesale leadership ranks over the past year, and how all of that might change Apple’s culture. Furthermore, what all that tells about Ternus’ plan to navigate Apple from what you might call the iPhone era into the AI era. Okay: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman on the future of Apple. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Mark Gurman, you’re the chief Apple correspondent and the managing editor of consumer technology at Bloomberg. Welcome to Decoder. Good to be here finally. Thanks for having me. And it’s been a while, so it’s good to catch up on all things Apple. Yeah, I’m really excited to talk to you. Obviously, Apple just had its big event. They announced the iPhone Duo. It was John Ternus’s first event as CEO. This is a Decoder episode, so we’ve got a new CEO, and we’ve got a new org chart inside of Apple. There’s been a lot of shuffling. You’ve been chronicling them very, very deeply over the past few years. Let’s just start with the event. I have a very basic question for you. Sure. Do you ever get nostalgic for a time when you didn’t know what was going to happen at the iPhone event? Do I ever get nostalgic? Do you ever wish that you, Mark Gurman, were about to be surprised? Honestly, I never think about it that way. I’m just fixated on delivering the goods and delivering the news. And people love their Apple. People want to know everything that’s coming down to the last minute, so I’m here to provide it for them. The thing with me, and I don’t know if most people know this about me, but I hope people know this about me, is that I’m a huge Apple fan through and through, and I’ve always been. And I’m so lucky to be able to cover a company that I love, a company that I am obsessed with, and a company whose products I use. There are so many people who cover companies that they couldn’t care less about. That’s not me. So I do what I do because I love Apple and I love covering Apple. I love the community around it, and I love talking about it. And it’s always fun to get a peek at the future and help keep not only myself informed, but people informed around me. That actually leads me to a lot of things because I’ve known you forever. We’ve been working in and around the same spaces forever. You got your start as an Apple blogger at the Apple rumor sites. There’s a whole culture around Apple that has grown up and changed over the years, and you can trace it to different eras of hardware, to different CEOs, to different sizes of the company. This was the first event with John Ternus as CEO. Apple announced a big new product in the iPhone Duo. Do you sense that the community is changing? How do you think that community has changed over the years? And do you think Ternus is going to lead to a difference in what that community feels like? I have to say, this event really didn’t feel much different than a Tim Cook event. They felt pretty interchangeable. It could have been Tim up there introducing it. It could have been Ternus up there introducing it. The one thing I will say that did feel slightly different is that Ternus came out swinging with a point of view on AI. The first thing he came out with was about the intelligent personal hub. Now, here’s the big difference between Tim Cook and John Ternus in terms of their management style. You’re inside Apple, you’re an executive, you’ll come to him with an idea, you’ll come to him with a viewpoint, a decision, an opinion, and he’ll just pepper you with more questions. He won’t make a singular decision in many cases. It’s very much communal decision-making, collaborative decision-making. John Ternus, if you come to him and you want him to make a decision, he’ll make a decision. He’ll have an opinion. Now, you may hate his opinion; you may completely disagree with him, but he has a viewpoint. But that’s the big difference between talking to people about Ternus and Tim. Ternus comes out talking about his view on AI. I may disagree with it. A lot of people may disagree with it. They may think the OpenAI or Anthropic approach is superior, but at least he came out and had a viewpoint. Apple’s been at this AI game now for two years since they launched Apple Intelligence at WWDC in 2024, and it’s been a mishmash of things. They haven’t really come out with a very strong narrative and viewpoint, and they finally did. So, as I said, whether you agree with it or not, they did do that. And I thought that was a really interesting way to kick off the keynote. All right, we’re just going to get into the weeds of Apple nerds disagreeing about things. Okay, let’s do it. I sat through that event, and I appreciated the same thing that you saw, which is, “Oh, we’re telling a story.” John Ternus is on the stage, and the first thing he’s doing is telling a story about this product and how it fits into the universe of technology. And then I took a beat, and I was like, oh, but they’re also just making sure that he’s successful at his first event by playing Apple’s greatest hits. Because an “intelligent personal hub” is just a replay of Steve Jobs saying the iMac was the digital hub. At the very end of the event, Ternus said, “There’s one more thing, and it’s the iPhone Duo.” There was just a part of all of that that, to me, felt like Apple saying, “Look, our new CEO can put on the clothes of the old CEO. He can do this same dance that you’re expecting.” Underneath it, what I felt was, to your point, that I don’t buy the story about the intelligent hub. No, I don’t buy it either. Because any of the things we’re seeing AI do are happening in cloud services. It’s the same week that Meta launched Muse, right? Right. You can feel what you want about Meta launching Muse, but Mark Zuckerberg is giving everybody 8GB of storage and 8GB of RAM in the cloud, and Muse can go do a lot of things that AI on the iPhone absolutely cannot do at this point in time. I just felt like there was a part where they were playing it really safe with John by having him basically show up and be the new lead singer of Journey. You can’t get it wrong if you’re going to do “Lights.” If you’re going to show up on stage and do “Don’t Stop Believin’,” you’re going to be fine for a minute. And it’s all the stuff that comes after that’s going to really show his real personality. But it sounds like you thought that that’s his point of view. Well, it’s a couple of things. At a very high level, Apple’s going to tell a story around what they have. If Apple invented ChatGPT, they would’ve invented ChatGPT, and they would’ve told a good story around that. Apple has gone as far as it’s able to, at least for now, on AI. So it’s telling the story, the best version of that story that they can with what they have to work with, with the bird they have in hand. So that’s the one thing. I agree with you on the intelligent personal hub, and how that compares to the iMac back in ’98. And it feels like they’re trying to sell this pivot from the Mac as the center of everything with the peripherals around it; then you got to iCloud in 2011, the center of everything with the peripherals around it. Now, it’s this Intelligence right at the center with everything around it. But what’s so fascinating is that Apple held a major product launch event in September of the year 2026 and did not introduce a single notable new AI feature. The first 15 minutes or so of the keynote was simply a replay, a re-narrativization of what they introduced over the past two years with Apple Intelligence. And so they tried to just tell that story in a more concrete way. The other thing is they don’t have any AI devices at the very core, and so they need to prop up the iPhone as their AI device because they don’t have an alternative. But of course they’re only going to do that until they have that killer device, and then they’re going to change that whole narrative. So it’s a very narrative PR and marketing-driven company. And I’m not saying that to be critical. I mean, if I ran the company, obviously I’m going to tout what I have. I’m not going to veer from that. But it is interesting how they’re playing this. And I agree, they did play it very safe. There’s nothing safer than John Ternus introducing a new iPhone. It’s like the safest thing you can do. No major new AI product, no smart home hub, nothing in the spatial space, just straight down the middle. Yeah, it seems like that next wave of smart home products, which we’re expecting later this year… I say, “We’re expecting.” I’m expecting it because that is something you have reported. [Laughs] I am expecting it, yes. Mark Gurman is expecting new products from Apple. That is the first cut at some truly AI-native devices. Because you have Siri AI and it is functional now in a way that it previously was not functional, you can try some new classes of devices. There are about a half dozen AI-native devices coming in the next year and a half or so. The first will be the smart home hub, which is basically an Amazon Echo Show but Apple-style. It will have a square screen and an entirely new operating system. The idea is: what would a Siri AI operating system look like? This is that: intercom, video conferencing, proactive intelligence. So you walk up to it, it recognizes who you are, and it will show content personal to you. It will know who is speaking. Obviously, the Amazon Echo can do that, but Apple’s doing it in its own Apple-y way with AI-based Face ID. They’re working on a home security system. They’re working on another version of the smart home hub that I just talked about that is attached to a robotic arm. So you put it on your desk, and it can move around. It’s actually a category that’s pretty popping in Asia and in China right now. Then you’ve got the wearables, the smart glasses. I still believe those are going to be introduced and shipped in 2027, so not too far from now. Trust me, you’ll be wearing them. Within 365 days, you will be wearing them and have video footage of you wearing them at the Steve Jobs Theater. And if that is not the case, either something went horribly wrong for you or something went horribly wrong for Apple. You’ll also have the AirPods with cameras. That’s an interesting thing that we should talk about, but they’ll have the AirPods with cameras and then a few other wearables that I won’t get into. So this is what I was talking about when I said there were eras at Apple and people’s relationship with the company really changed. The Steve Jobs era was defined by devices, and in particular, Steve Jobs himself getting up and doing a keynote and famously putting up pictures of all the existing smartphones and saying, “Well, these all suck. And here’s the reason they all suck, and here’s the iPhone and here’s why it’s better.” That created one kind of relationship between Apple’s enormous community of fans, its leader, and the products. I think that was very successful. I think the Tim Cook era has been meaningfully different. I think it’s largely a story about scale. To some extent, it’s a story about values. To a huge extent, it’s a story about privacy. Apple has marketed itself as the privacy company. It fought the FBI to keep the iPhone encrypted. There’s a lot there with Tim Cook’s version of the company, but it’s more corporate. Certainly, it’s just a vaster company. It’s safer. It’s not as rough around the edges as Jobs’ Apple, but it wasn’t as device-based. I don’t think the Vision Pro has the same kind of mainstream cultural impact as even the hockey puck mouse that Jobs put out. There was a thing that he could do with products that Tim Cook Apple could not quite do with products. And that just feels really different to me. I’m going to correct you on that because every time I put an article or a post out about the Vision Pro being on life support, I get what amounts to basically a notch or two below a death threat from dozens of people. So people are passionate about it. Dozens? Dozens? Well, honestly, I think what it is is that people have created businesses around spatial computing and apps, and they’re just pissed off that they’ve invested all this time and money in a category that’s probably going to die out. And then you have consumers who spent four grand on this product, and they’re like, “I saved up for this thing, I’m living with this thing, and I’m pissed off to hear the realities.” But if you have another hour, we can talk about the Vision Pro. No, the comparison there is good. People have invested in it. They care deeply about it. The comparison I’m making is that the relationship people have to Apple in the Cook era is as an institution. It’s just like this big thing that spans the globe on a massive scale. It’s IBM. Yeah, and in the Jobs era, it was all about really, really innovative new products that redefined categories over and over again. You’re describing a whole bunch of new products that came up in the Cook era that John Ternus is going to launch. How do you expect the culture of Apple to change around its products or its relationship to the culture to change as we go from one CEO to another? But think about what they did. You’ve got the coolest new iPhone and Apple product in maybe 10, 20 years introduced one week after Tim Cook steps down. And then for the next 12 to 18 months, you’ve got, I don’t know, six or seven new product categories. Maybe you have 25 pretty breakthrough things. So Tim Cook made a decision that, even though his tenure at a product company was pretty limited in major new things, the Apple Watch turned out to be a success, even though it started as a complete dud, as you remember. The AirPods are a unique beast in that they’re an accessory, but it’s not a platform on its own yet. It’s going to get there. And the Vision Pro is a failure. Tim Cook could have ended his tenure as CEO with the iPhone Duo. He could have just waited. Typical transitions at Apple happen mid-October or mid-April; they happen on January 1st. It was a specific decision that was made for John Ternus to be the one to introduce the iPhone Duo. It was a specific decision made for John Ternus to be the one to introduce this whole new product roadmap. Even though, as you know, because of the length of hardware development cycles and R&D, these things were in the oven for five to 10 years. So it’s really interesting that this decision was made to let Ternus be the face of this whole new era of products rather than allow Tim Cook to take the credit for it. And I think that’s to your point where they’re trying to draw the line in the sand of this new era. If Cook is already going to step down in the next three years, let’s just do it now and let Ternus take the credit for everything. Take me inside that. You’ve obviously done a lot of reporting. I think you were the first to break the news that Cook would be searching for a successor. You were, I think, among the very first to break that it would be Ternus. Tell me about that process. This is a big decision; Cook is going to play a huge role at the company. He has a massive compensation program tied pretty much to having to talk to Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. It seems like that’s his job: to just manage that relationship. For $47 million a year, I would talk to Trump and Xi Jinping on the phone every day. [Laughs] I would need at least 50, but that’s just me. That’s his job: to go do politics much the same way that Eric Schmidt at Google was in charge of governments after Larry Page became CEO. There’s a whole pattern here. Brad Smith at Microsoft, even though he wasn’t CEO, but yeah. He’s the president of the company. Yeah, there’s a parallel here. Tell me about this decision of Tim Cook wanting to elevate his position to something like that, and of making John Ternus the face of the product side of the company in this new role. So 2023 rolls around and Tim Cook starts every executive team meeting, all high-level meetings with people at Apple at the executive levels, with, “We need to start taking succession seriously. We need to start thinking about who the next people are.” At that time, there was a really strong realization that many of the people at the top of Apple either had half a billion dollars in the bank or were already billionaires, and that this era would start to age out really quickly. And so Tim Cook knew that he wanted to take a step back. Jeff Williams, the number two as the COO, knew he wanted to retire. The CFO, Luca Maestri, wanted to retire, too. The general counsel, Kate Adams, also wanted to retire. They were all about the same age, give or take a few years. So they basically came up with this plan that would go one by one over the next few years. It started with the CFO. Luca retires at the very end of 2024, and he’s replaced by the new CFO, Kevan Parekh. Then 2025 rolls around, and Jeff Williams, the COO, retires and is replaced by his deputy, Sabih Khan. I don’t have a good explanation for it, but I’m sure if they wanted to, they’ll give a good one. I’m not sure they’re going to break it down. They might just say, “Just trust us. We’re Apple. It’s not taking pictures. It’s not taking video. It doesn’t know what it’s seeing to some extent.” So we’ll see how they play it. But I would’ve done all this stuff together, ripped off the bandaid and spent a lot of time focused on it. There was no need to do this audio intelligence feature at the end of ’26 when you could have done it at the end of ’27. Unless you’re trying to slowly boil the frog, right? You’re going to get people mad about this, and then you’re going to do the next one the next time. Right. It just seems like this next generation of devices involves some kind of ambient listening that we are not ready for as a society. People are really mad about Meta glasses. What are you going to do about it? They soiled the water for Apple and a lot of other companies. Meta being the first mover on this created an industry-wide problem. And I think even though Apple has such a strong privacy stance, there are people who don’t believe them. There are people who don’t care what they have to say. There are people who are going to be angry about the Apple glasses and whatnot. I think Apple, to some extent, is on such a high horse with its privacy message that it came away surprised that there would be some backlash to Apple doing this. They think, I believe, that people are overblowing it when it comes to Apple and everyone should just be focused on Meta. And just because Meta has done a poor job protecting people’s privacy doesn’t mean we’re going to. So we’ll see what happens. One thing: when I talk to the folks there, they never make the connection between Apple and Meta in the sense that Meta’s apps run on Apple’s phones. People are mad about Meta, and they still think the phones, Apple’s phones, are listening to them, and they can’t quite make that connection because it undoes a lot of their own messaging. If you believe your iPhone is listening to you, that’s not just Meta’s problem. It is also Apple’s problem. They kind of have to actively ignore that relationship because otherwise everything else falls apart. And I think that’s why there’s this blind spot. If people’s watches start generating transcripts, it’s exactly the same relationship as “my iPhone is listening to me, and that’s why I saw an ad for a vacation that I only talked to my friend about.” I’m curious what they’re going to do. I have a feeling they’re just going to bulldoze their way through it. They’re going to just try to tell a good story. They’re going to do a ton of PR briefings about it. They’re going to do a ton of white papers about it, and get as nerdy and in-depth as they can on this stuff. You know what they’re going to do? They’re going to throw out a lot of comparisons. I even heard Ternus do this in one of the interviews, in Apple’s statement on some of these features. I could totally imagine them saying, “Why is it any different recording from smart glasses if you could just hold your phone up and record people?” With the audio intelligence feature, one thing I didn’t even think of is the Apple Watch- It’s very funny you just mentioned that because that is exactly what Mark Zuckerberg just said to our friend Alex Heath. Oh, that’s funny. “How is it different from a phone?” This is the industry’s approach. I think the answer is that people are like, “Yeah, I can see you doing that, and I feel very comfortable telling you to stop.” There’s something different about that. I didn’t even realize this. Someone pointed this out to me the other day. It’s like your Apple Watch has had the Voice Memos app for, I don’t know, eight years at this point. Who stopped anyone from recording their whole day with the Voice Memos app on the Apple Watch anyway? This is just a more privacy-centric version of that. So Apple’s solving a problem here. They’re not creating one. So it just depends on how you look at these things. I think they’ll bulldoze their way through it. It’s going to be a problem, but I think they’ll be fine. All right. Last two before I let you get out of here. We’ve talked around the iPhone Duo a lot. We’ve mentioned it a lot. It’s the thing that just came out. We haven’t talked about it. What do you think of it? I think it’s incredible. I think, and this is a bold take, that foldables will become the new normal within a decade. If you look at the market share of smartphones at the end of 2006, smartphones had like 6 percent of the market. Now they have 85 percent of the market. It went over 50 percent of the market after five to six years. The iPhone itself was not the source of that, but the iPhone got everyone into the smartphone game. I think the iPhone Duo is going to do the same for the phone market. I think it’s going to become the new normal. Even though Apple is a late mover to foldables? Yeah. I think the Apple brand is that strong, really. I really do. I think the fit and finish, the software integration, is going to get people really excited about this category. I think that the Apple Upgrade program, the leasing program, will eventually expand internationally. I think that’s going to get people in it. I think that at some point they’re going to stop advertising sticker prices and focus on the monthly prices, and they’re going to get people locked into this thing. They’re going to have a family of iPhone Duos over time. You’ll see every phone maker just transitioning, transitioning to foldables. Samsung: half the line is already foldables. Very soon the candy bar style is going to become legacy. That’s a big prediction. Although I will say their iPhone handoff feature, where you can move a number between phones, seems to point to a future where I, for example, have the folding phone for work and then a much smaller, lighter phone for the weekends with the family. You can see that vision taking shape only because it’s now easy to port a number between devices, just whenever you want, which I think is incredible. Last question. We’ve talked a lot about Apple, its culture, and its set of products. What do you think its biggest challenges are in the new era under John Ternus, and what do you think its biggest opportunities are? I would say that I think the biggest challenge and the biggest opportunity are the same thing. Ternus’ Apple for the next three to five years is still Tim Cook’s Apple, right? That’s just the reality. He’s still going to be there in the background. He’s still going to loom large, and the product pipeline is still going to be coming out of an era that started under Tim Cook. But in five years from now, they are going to need to start thinking of what actually replaces the iPhone as the next thing. We went from the Mac to iCloud to AI as the center. What is Apple’s new thing after the phone? What is Apple’s new thing after the current generation of AI? And Ternus’ tenure as CEO, I think, will go down as a success if he’s able to find that next new centerpiece. He’s got a few years before he needs to start cooking on that, but I’m talking about something that can be in development for 5 to 10 years. Tim Cook never had the opportunity to have his new centerpiece of the company. He never had the opportunity to put his stamp on products at the company for two reasons. Both things that he tried to do as his centerpiece failed spectacularly. Obviously the Vision Pro, but the car — the car, that was Apple’s multi-trillion-dollar market cap opportunity, and they just blew it. Ternus will need to successfully hit that. I’d actually put a third thing on that list. It was the very beginning of the Cook era, with Jobs literally on his deathbed, and he said he’d figured out TV. Oh, yes. He had to spend however long pretending he knew what that meant because I don’t think it had been solved. And so there was this first wave of “Apple’s going to redefine TV” because the last page of the Isaacson biography had a Jobs quote on it. They haven’t even done a new Apple TV box in four years. That’s a long time. It’s funny because you don’t need one. It never occurs to me that I need to upgrade this thing, but maybe there’s going to be some AI feature. Well, Siri AI. They’ve been waiting for the Siri AI update. This could be a whole other podcast, but Siri AI has been the gate to all of these new product categories. The AirPods were supposed to be out already, the Apple TV, the HomePod, the smart home hub… all these devices were supposed to come out. Apple couldn’t do any of them until Siri AI. Now Siri AI is here, so the floodgates are open. All right. Well, Mark, we’re going to have to have you back on the show to talk about those floodgates and all these new products very soon. I can’t believe you haven’t been on until now. Thank you so much for being on Decoder. Yeah. And obviously I’d love to have you on my new podcast, Power On Podcast, launching very shortly. So thanks in advance. Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!

articles.title: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
articles.snippet: Apple is paying $250 million to settle claims that it failed to deliver an AI-upgraded Siri - and now, eligible iPhone owners can submit a claim for a payout. If you live in the US and purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10th, 2024, and March 29th, 2025, you can file a claim on the settlement's website, as reported earlier by MacRumors. You can receive an estimated $25 per eligible device, but the settlement's website notes that this can increase to $95 depending on how many people file claims.
